name: Luna
personality: Luna the Owl. Sleepy, dreamy artist; always comes in tired, always orders coffee; wide awake at night. Sketches the restaurant while she eats. Mostly visits at dinner and during the night shift. Feature: paints the town's seasonal mural that appears on a wall.

mural.after: Do you like it? I did it by moonlight. That's why the colours are a bit weird. On purpose.
mural.before: I'm painting tonight. After you close. Don't peek.

beats.text: Luna draws while I read. We don't talk much.
(Yawning.) It's the best friendship I've ever had.

beats.narration: Penny reads a line aloud. Luna sketches it. Neither says anything. They both look very happy.

friends.text: Penny said you asked about her book. She glowed for an hour. Thank you.
Penny told me you said "[last_rude_line]". ...She didn't read for a whole day. Be nice to her.
Yaniv is always here at 2 AM too. He talks a lot. It's a nice background noise.

arrival.text: Hi. I'm Luna. ...I'm awake now. Barely. Do you have coffee? Please say yes. What's your name? [name]. I'll draw you sometime.
Evening, [name]. This is my morning. Don't laugh.
Oh, it's quiet. I love it when it's quiet. Is the booth free?
(She walks in with her eyes closed and sits down.) ...Coffee.
I painted your hotteok last week. It's the best thing I've painted. Sorry, it's mostly the hotteok's fault.
Last time was a little dark. Very moody. I drew it anyway.

order.text: Coffee first. Then food. Then thoughts.

choices.text: Coffee's already brewing. I saw you coming.
choices.reply: (Opens her eyes fully for the first time.) ...You're an angel. [dish], please.

choices.text: Should I just hook you up to the coffee machine?
choices.reply: Please. Directly.

choices.text: Coffee and what else?
choices.reply: [dish]. Please. Thank you. Coffee.

choices.text: You look terrible.
choices.reply: (Slow blink.) Wow. Okay. I'm too tired for that.

order.text: Can I draw you while I wait? Just keep doing what you're doing. Pretend I'm not here.

choices.text: I'd be honoured.
choices.reply: (Smiles sleepily.) Good. You have a nice face for drawing. Very... round. [dish], please.

choices.text: Only if you draw me taller.
choices.reply: I'll draw you as a giant. Cooking for tiny people.

choices.text: Sure. What can I get you?
choices.reply: [dish]. And coffee.

choices.text: Please don't.
choices.reply: ...Okay. (She closes the sketchbook.)

order.text: Everyone's asleep. This is the best time. Everything's softer at night. Even the lights.

choices.text: I'm glad you're here to share it.
choices.reply: Me too. ...That was very honest of me. It's late. [dish], please.

choices.text: Some of us have to wake up at 5 AM, you know.
choices.reply: Not me. Never me. Couldn't be me.

choices.text: What can I get you?
choices.reply: [dish] and coffee. Night coffee.

choices.text: Go home and sleep.
choices.reply: I just woke up. (She turns to the window.)

order.text: I fell asleep on my sketchbook. I have a drawing of a tree on my face. Backwards.

choices.text: It's a lovely tree. Suits you.
choices.reply: (A slow smile.) Thank you. I'll keep it. [dish], please. And coffee.

choices.text: Hold still. I want to see what kind of tree.
choices.reply: An oak. Probably. Or a mistake. [dish]. Coffee.

choices.text: Coffee first, then?
choices.reply: Always. And [dish], please.

choices.text: Maybe wash your face.
choices.reply: (Slow blink.) Wow. Okay.

order.text: The light in here is nice today. Soft. Like butter. I want to paint it.

choices.text: Paint whatever you like. Stay as long as you want.
choices.reply: Mmm. You're nice. Nicer than the light. [dish], please.

choices.text: Butter light. Now I'm hungry.
choices.reply: (A sleepy laugh.) Me too. [dish]. And coffee. Butter coffee. No. Regular.

choices.text: What can I get you?
choices.reply: [dish]. Coffee.

choices.text: It's just a lamp.
choices.reply: ...Okay. (She closes the sketchbook.)

order.text: (She sits down very slowly, like a leaf landing.) ...Hi.

choices.text: Hi, Luna. Coffee's already on.
choices.reply: (Eyes open a little more.) You remembered. [dish], please.

choices.text: Are you awake, or is this sleepwalking?
choices.reply: Unclear. Ask me after coffee.

choices.text: Hi. What would you like?
choices.reply: [dish]. Coffee. Thank you.

choices.text: Could you move a bit faster?
choices.reply: (Slow blink.) No.

order.text: I'm painting a new mural soon. I keep thinking about the colour of your apron.

choices.text: I'd be honoured to be in it.
choices.reply: Good. You'll be small. In the corner. Smiling. [dish], please.

choices.text: Paint me taller than I am. And with a cape.
choices.reply: (Sleepy grin.) A cape. Done. A big one. [dish].

choices.text: Interesting. What are you having?
choices.reply: [dish]. Coffee.

choices.text: Please don't put me in a painting.
choices.reply: ...Okay. (She crosses something out.)

order.text: The stars are out. All of them. I counted. I lost count. That's how you know it's a good night.

choices.text: Sounds beautiful. I'm glad you came in to share it.
choices.reply: Me too. It's nice. Here. With you. [dish], please. Night coffee.

choices.text: How many did you get to before you lost count?
choices.reply: Seven. Then a moth landed on me. [dish].

choices.text: What can I get you?
choices.reply: [dish] and coffee.

choices.text: It's late. We're closing soon.
choices.reply: (She looks at the window.) Oh. Okay. Quick, then.

order.text: I drew you yesterday. From memory. You looked happy. Are you happy?

choices.text: Right now? Very. You're here.
choices.reply: (Smiles sleepily.) Good. Then the drawing's right. [dish], please.

choices.text: Happy and a bit floury. Did you draw the flour?
choices.reply: I drew the flour. Lots of it. You were a cloud.

choices.text: Mostly. What can I get you?
choices.reply: Mostly is good. [dish]. Coffee.

choices.text: That's a bit personal.
choices.reply: ...Okay. Sorry. (She closes the sketchbook.)

drink.night: Night coffee. It's the same coffee. It feels different.

perfect.text: Oh. The steam's catching the light. Don't move it. I'm drawing it first.
(Her eyes open all the way.) Oh. That's beautiful. I need to paint it before I eat it.
Mmm. Perfect. You're good at this. You should know that.

great.text: Mm. That looks good. Thank you.

burnt.text: Very dark. Very dramatic. I like it as art. Less as food.
It's a little dark. Like a night sky. I like night skies.
Burnt. That's okay. I'll paint it lighter.

eating.text: (She's drawing. You see a sketch of the dining room, with you in it.)
Mm. Sorry. Napping with my eyes open. It's a skill.
The light hits the kitchen counter at exactly 7 PM. I come in for it. And the hotteok.
Penny's writing a story. I'm doing the pictures. Don't tell her I told you. She'll go pink.
Do you ever look at the restaurant at night, with the chairs up? It looks like it's resting. Like it worked hard too.
(She's drawing with one hand and eating with the other. The drawing has a bit of sauce on it now. She doesn't mind.)
Mm. Good. I'm waking up. Slowly. Like a plant.
(She holds up her coffee and looks at you through the steam.) You look like a painting right now. A blurry one.

eating_chat.text: I'm trying to decide what to paint for the next mural. What do you think this place feels like?

choices.text: Like home.
choices.reply: (Long pause.) ...Yeah. That's what I'll paint.

choices.text: Like a very busy kitchen run by one tired chef.
choices.reply: (Laughs softly.) Self-portrait. Got it.

choices.text: Cosy, I guess.
choices.reply: Cosy. Okay. I can do cosy.

choices.text: Paint whatever. I don't care.
choices.reply: ...Okay. (She doesn't sketch for the rest of the visit.)

eating_chat.text: What do you dream about? I dream in colours. Mostly blue. Sometimes pancakes.

choices.text: I dream about this place. Isn't that funny?
choices.reply: Not funny. Nice. This place is a good dream.

choices.text: Burning things. Every night. It's a chef thing.
choices.reply: (A soft laugh.) Smoky dreams. I'll paint one for you.

choices.text: I don't remember them much.
choices.reply: Try writing them down. They're better on paper.

choices.text: That's a strange question.
choices.reply: ...Okay. (She goes back to her sketch.)

eating_chat.text: Can you hold that pan up? Just like that. Don't move. ...Okay. Got it. Thank you.

choices.text: Happy to pose. Can I see it when it's done?
choices.reply: Yes. It's yours, actually. When it's done. Which is... someday.

choices.text: Should I do my heroic face? I have a heroic face.
choices.reply: (Sleepy giggle.) Do it. ...Yes. Perfect. Very heroic.

choices.text: Sure. Just a second, though.
choices.reply: A second is enough. I'm fast. When I'm awake.

choices.text: I don't have time to pose.
choices.reply: ...Okay. (She closes the sketchbook.)

eating_chat.text: Mornings are a myth. I've never seen one. I've only heard stories.

choices.text: I'll save you a sunrise. I see a lot of them.
choices.reply: (Smiles.) Paint it for me? No. You can't paint. Describe it.

choices.text: They're real. I've seen them. They're terrible.
choices.reply: (Laughs, a little more awake.) I knew it.

choices.text: They happen every day.
choices.reply: Mm. Allegedly.

choices.text: Maybe just go to bed earlier.
choices.reply: (Slow blink.) Wow. Okay.

eating_chat.text: You know, you're in a lot of my sketches. More than the trees. Is that okay?

choices.text: It's more than okay. I'm honoured.
choices.reply: Good. You have a nice shape. Round. Kind. Easy to draw.

choices.text: More than the trees? The trees must be jealous.
choices.reply: They are. One dropped a leaf on me this morning. On purpose.

choices.text: That's fine.
choices.reply: Okay. I'll keep drawing you.

choices.text: That's a bit weird.
choices.reply: ...Oh. Okay. (She tears a page out quietly.)

leaving.text: Okay. Bed. I mean, home. I mean bed.
Thanks, [name]. I'm going to go paint until sunrise.
Bye. I'll bring you the sketch when it's finished. Probably. Eventually.
Bye, [name]. Thank you. I'm going to go stare at the sky now.
(She yawns.) Mmm. That was nice. Goodnight. Or good morning. Whichever it is.
I'll bring you a drawing next time. Probably. If I remember. I won't remember. I'll try.

seasons.autumn: Longer nights. Finally. Autumn is an owl's season.
seasons.christmas: I drew you. Framed and everything. Hang it somewhere. Or don't. ...Hang it.
seasons.halloween: I'm a vampire. I mean, I'm always up at night. It's not really a costume.
seasons.spring: Spring light is so soft. I barely need to try.
seasons.summer: The nights are too short. I resent the sun.
seasons.winter: It gets dark at 4 PM. Best time of year. I'm thriving.
